thread:
lee: hey everyone — i'm lee, just joined infra. accepted the org invite but when i try to clone a private repo i get a 403 `Permission to redwood-inference/platform.git denied to lee123`. i'm listed in the platform team in the org UI and i set up an authenticator app for 2FA. any ideas?

alex: welcome lee! quick Q — are you using SSH or HTTPS to clone? and what's your github username?

lee: username is lee123. i'm using SSH (added my key to GH profile). exact git error: `fatal: Could not read from remote repository.` remote side: `Permission to redwood-inference/platform.git denied to lee123.`

alex: ok can you run `ssh -T git@github.com` and paste output (sanitized) so we can confirm key auth?

lee: output: `Hi lee123! You've successfully authenticated, but GitHub does not provide shell access.`

alex: SSH auth looks fine. most likely it's an SSO/SAML authorization issue or email mismatch. Does the org require SAML SSO?

lee: i think so — i see an SSO banner on the org page, i clicked it but the "Authorize" button was greyed out for me.

irene: hey @lee — devex here. greyed out authorize usually means your GitHub account primary email doesn't match the corporate email we invited. can you check your GitHub Settings -> Emails and confirm if your work email (lee@redwood.ai) is listed and verified?

lee: i just checked — my profile primary email is lee.personal@gmail.com. i didn't realize that would block SSO.

irene: yep, org SSO often maps via verified emails. easiest fix: add your work email to your GH account, verify it (you'll get a verification link), then try the org -> Authorize SSO flow again. steps: 1) Settings > Emails > Add `lee@redwood.ai` 2) click verification link 3) go to https://github.com/orgs/redwood-inference/sso and click Authorize. if the button is still greyed out after verify, tell us and we can re-send the invite tied to that email.

lee: adding and verifying now...

onboard-bot: reminder: new-hire checklist — verify corporate email for GitHub SSO (item 3/12).

lee: ok i added lee@redwood.ai and verified it. i went back to the SSO page and clicked Authorize — it succeeded. i retried `git clone` and it worked :tada:

alex: awesome. one more thing — repo-level write access might still be restricted. by default platform team is read-only for some repos. ping @irene if you need push rights and tell her which repo.

lee: @irene can you add me to the platform-writers team for redwood-inference/platform.git?

irene: done — added you to platform-writers and gave repo-level write. try a push when you're ready.

lee: push worked. thanks so much everyone :thumbsup:

alex: welcome aboard and congrats on surviving the first infrastructure hiccup :) FYI if you ever see your membership as "Outside collaborator" instead of org member, reach out to people-ops/devex — sometimes the invite was sent to a different email and needs re-linking.

lee: noted. thanks again!
